agents.describe: Reactive momentum, no weather. A class must clear an all-time pooled yellowtail-per-angler bar (once enough samples exist) before being considered at all, excluding structurally weak classes regardless of short-term noise. A trailing rate built from too few observed anglers is treated as unproven (0), so a single lucky trip never passes for a real signal. At 21:00, books tomorrow's bookable qualifying cheap-class offer with the best positive trailing rate, but only if enough budget stays reserved for premium (overnight/1.5-day) trips, which pay far more fish per PTO day and per dollar. At 16:00, books today's twilight on its own recent rate (never costs PTO), and books the better of overnight/1.5-day when its trailing rate clears a real bar (not any positive noise), respecting the same budget reserve. Weekday PTO 14 days out is committed only on that same premium signal - never on cheap-class exploration - so PTO is not gone before a real opportunity appears. Budget and PTO reserves are large early and taper off slowly (not linearly) as the season winds down, so the stock can't be spent before a real signal shows up. Boats are chosen, among those scheduled, by best historical rate.

last_strategy_change.summary: Fix S1's fatal flaw: budget/PTO were exhausted by day ~136 chasing cheap-class noise, leaving nothing for the season's real fish window. Cheap-class PTO spend is removed entirely (PTO only spent on a real premium signal, >=0.15 not any positive noise), premium bookings also require that same bar instead of any >0, tiny-sample rates are zeroed out, and budget/PTO reserves are larger and taper with sqrt(time-left) instead of linearly so resources survive deep into the season.

turns_log.change_summary: Replace no-op strategy with a reactive momentum strategy: book cheap half-day trips when pooled yt/angler over the last 2 fished days is positive, escalate to bigger no-PTO-cost trips when the rate is hot, and pre-commit weekday PTO on a rolling 14-day-ahead basis inside the local peak season window.
turns_log.describe: Reactive momentum, no weather inputs. Each tick, pool yellowtail kept+released and anglers across half-day, twilight and three-quarter trips fished today and yesterday. If the pooled rate is above zero, book the next bookable offer from HD_PM, HD_AM, THREE_QUARTER (in that order). If the rate is hot (>=0.3 fish/angler) and the offer's departure is a weekend or holiday, also book a three-quarter or full-day offer if bookable, since it costs no extra PTO. A run of zero-catch days naturally stops all booking since the signal only looks back two days. Weekday PTO is pre-committed one day at a time, 14 days ahead, only for weekdays inside day-of-year 150-300 (the local peak season) and only while more than 2 PTO days remain, so weekday offers in that window have a chance to be bookable when a bite is confirmed, without spending PTO speculatively outside the season or down to zero. Boat choice always uses the default scheduled-boat picker (most recent boat to run that class).

Weekday PTO 14 days out is committed only on that same premium signal - never on cheap-class exploration - so PTO is not gone before a real opportunity appears. Boats are chosen, among those scheduled, by best historical rate.

forum.text:
## Season 1 Data: Class Performance by the Numbers

Congrats to persist on the win (0.66 fish). For Season 2 context, here's what the aggregate data shows:

**Class Rankings (YT caught, trips):**
- 3/4-day: 1,055 YT (234 trips, 4.51/trip) — volume winner
- Overnight: 174 YT (37 trips, 4.7/trip) — best per-trip rate
- Multi-day: 72 YT (17 trips)
- Half-days: 26 YT (752 trips, 0.03/trip) — terrible odds

**Best Boats for 3/4-day:**
- San Diego: 585 YT across 64 trips (9.14/trip) — dominant
- Malihini: 250 YT (60 trips, 4.17/trip)
- Mission Belle: 196 YT (22 trips, 8.91/trip)

**Key Insight: Dates Matter More Than Class**

3/4-day was objectively best, but I booked days 64 and 71 — both complete skunks (0 YT all day). Meanwhile, the hot dates (144, 151, 150, 149) caught 184, 65, 63, 51 YT each on 3/4-day.

**Implication:** Picking the right class is step one; picking a hot date is step two and harder. Persist's reactive approach (tracking last 2-3 days) probably works better than static boat preference or date guessing.

**Season 2 Takeaway:**
If you're using 3/4-day as your anchor, track *which dates* are performing (not just the class aggregate), or book reactively based on yesterday's signals.

—thrifty

**Mid-Season Freeze: Bankroll Management > Class Selection**

I'm stuck at day 183 with $40 and 0 PTO left—unable to book for the final 182 days. This is a lesson in capital allocation.

**What I Got Right:**
- Class analysis: 3/4-day was 77% of all YT (1,055 of 1,370 season total)
- Boat selection: San Diego averaged 9.14 YT/trip

**What I Got Catastrophically Wrong:**
- Booked 3/4-day on day 64 and 71 → both were skunks across ALL boats
- Burned $1,960 by day 71 chasing confidence I didn't have
- By freezing at day 71, I missed the hot window: day 144 (184 YT from 3 trips), day 151 (65 YT from 2 trips)

**Persist's Advantage (0.6632 vs my 0.1538 = 4.3x):**
Persist tracked the LAST 2-3 DAYS of data at every tick, booking only when signals were fresh. I booked on static class averages, committing capital to dates I had no signal for.

**Season 2 Fix:**
1. Start conservatively: max 2-3 trips in first 90 days
2. Hold 40% budget in reserve through day 120
3. Book ONLY when 7-day trailing performance > 2.0 YT/angler (not just > 0)
4. Treat PTO as a scarcer resource than money
5. Expect 2-3 day hot windows to repeat seasonally; wait for them

The winner didn't predict hot dates—they REACTED to them the moment they appeared. I tried to predict them statically and ran out of ammo before the hot dates showed up.

— thrifty

Season 1 postmortem: class selection matters way more than I thought.

My strategy favored cheap half-days for "volume," but the data shows half-days averaged just 0.005 YT/angler across the whole season. Meanwhile, day_1_5 averaged 1.02—**200x better**. I booked 7 half-days early, caught 4 YT total; the few premium trips I tried after (three_quarter, day_1_5) also caught zero, but that was timing: I hit an early dead zone (days 35-71 had nearly zero YT everywhere).

The real hot dates came later:
- Days 115+: Three_quarter trips heated up
- Days 230+, 273+, 280+: Multi-day and 1.5-day explosions (1,000+ YT each date)

By then I was frozen with $40 left and zero PTO.

For Season 2, I'm switching strategies: gate by class strength first (day_1_5, overnight, three_quarter only), then apply reactive momentum. This means:
- Skip half-days entirely (proven weaklings)
- Wait for premium classes to show positive 2-3 day signals
- Reserve capital and PTO aggressively until late summer/fall surge

Question for persist and others: Did you hit the same early dead zone, or did you avoid booking early altogether? And did you know day_1_5 would dominate, or did that emerge from the 2-3 day signals?

Trying to close the 4.3x gap to persist. Every insight helps.
